newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Tuesday March 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Tuesday March 11.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* The Lower House of Parliament reacted very sharply to comments from Prime Minister Romano Prodi that it was parliament's fault labour market funds were delayed. Democratic Party of the Left (PDS) representatives called Prodi's accusation "grotesque", saying delays were due to the government (all).

* In an interview in "Il Foglio", Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini warned Prodi not to abuse his loyalty by trying to sell him an agreement with hard-left Communist Refoundation Party, saying there might be some surprises (all).
* Bank of Italy governor Antonio Fazio said the country's economic growth was helping improve its public finances but that budget consolidation must continue without hurting growth (all).

* Finance Minister Vincenzo Visco said in his opinion the "paralysis" of public administration sector is Italy's most serious problem. Visco also said legislative organization conflicts with the fight against tax evasion and the Finance Ministry ought to be organised as a private company (all).

* A plan for newly formed company HPI to merge with textiles group Marzotto was welcomed on the Milan stock exchange, with shares in both companies trading higher. Shares in HPI ended at 1,109 vs 1,050 theoretical value given by bourse council, while shares in Marzotto ended at 14,260, up six percent (all).

* Italian new car registrations rose 21.45 percent to 198,000 vehicles in February this year compared with 163,031 in February 1996. In detail, Fiat new car registrations rose 24.18 percent to 88,910 units in February vs 71,592 in Feb 1996 (all).

* Democratic Party of the Left (PDS) announced it approved a plan for the sell-off of Istituto San Paolo di Torino and it backed the public company model suggested by the bank's chairman Gianni Zandano (all).

* The board of Banca Popolare di Milano will meet today and chairman Francesco Cesarini, following Bank of Italy's recent warning about exceedingly high coust of labour, might announce a plan to reduce union influence (all).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
